This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. The National Hurricane Center has downgraded Hurricane Isaias to a post-tropical cyclone as its remnants moved north over Alabama and Georgia.
More than 700,000 customers are now without power across the region. NPR's Matt Bloom has more.
Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane near Destin, Florida late Friday. It packed 105 mile-an-hour winds.
Multiple emergency management agencies across the region have reported downed trees and power lines,
and many have urged residents to remain sheltered in place while crews work to clear roads.
Isaias was the first hurricane of this Atlantic season, and its remnants are expected to bring damaging winds and heavy rainfall across the southeast as it moves more inland.
That's NPR's Matt Bloom with our reports.
Hours after an international humanitarian legal expert was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, the State Department announced sanctions on the International Criminal Court.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio has vowed to dismantle the world's only standing war crimes tribunal, as NPR's Michelle Kelliman reports.
Secretary Rubio says the U.S. will ban transactions with what he calls a "rogue court," cutting off its resources and crippling its ability to operate.
America never joined the court. We don't need that court, and we don't want it.
The ICC was set up as a court of last resort for victims of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.
The U.S. protested an investigation into Afghanistan, which could have implicated U.S. service members.
The ICC closed that investigation.
The U.S. also opposes the arrest warrant against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the war in Gaza.
The ICC says in a statement that it will not be deterred, but its fate now rests in the hands of the states that created it.
Michelle Kelliman, NPR News, Washington.
Secretary of Homeland Security Mark Wayne Mullen says ICE officers did not know a five-year-old boy was in the car when they surrounded and shot a Dominican man in New York City on Thursday night.
As NPR's Nate Perez reports, officers fired as many as seven rounds.
ICE shot Oscar Belga on the neck when he was pulling into a parking space.
Mullen says ICE wasn't aware a child was in the car, but he says that Belga accelerated his speed and ramped two vehicles.
Mullen also alleges Belga appeared to target officers with his car.
The public outcry should be also towards this criminal, this thug, this gangbanger, this possible murderer.
Belga was treated at a hospital but has been moved to a detention center outside New York.
New York Mayor Zoran Mamdani and Governor Kathy Hochul denounced ICE and demanded they pause their operations.
But Mullen has vowed to continue. Nate Perez, NPR News.
Stocks finished up on Wall Street on Friday, and you're listening to NPR News.
Friday, the Crown Estate, which manages assets for the British monarchy, revealed some of its accounting related to King Charles's disgraced brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, from London, and Pierre's lawyer in Freyrd reports.
Ex-Prince Andrew was evicted earlier this year from a royal lodge near Windsor Castle amid public anger over his ties to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Now the Crown Estate says it found nearly $2.4 million of what it calls "delapidations" to the lodge.
Some of that came from a $400,000 refund Andrew got from vacating his lease early, the Crown Estate notes.
But an official familiar with palace accounts who asked not to be identified because they're not authorized to speak publicly about them says most of the money, nearly $2 million, came from King Charles himself in the form of a loan to his brother.
Andrew settled a lawsuit with one of Epstein's victims and remains under police investigation for allegedly sharing government secrets with Epstein, but denies any wrongdoing.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, London.
Life in the Brazilian city of Manos is being disrupted this weekend because of unhealthy air caused by smoke from wildfires in the Amazon, the city's suspended in-person work at municipal offices.
The concentration of pollutants is averaging 196 micrograms per cubic meter. The normal range is from 3 to 9 micrograms.
In college football, Bear Bachmeier passed for 329 yards and two touchdowns and ran for a career-best 109 rushing yards as No. 8 BYU beat Iowa State Friday night 24 to 10.
No. 20 Iowa easily handled Washington 41 to 24 and Louisville scored a comeback win over Florida State.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
